criteria.rationale: Peaks with s >= 100 must essentially always be found; 1 % allows a pathological realisation near the analysis-range boundary.

Gaussian peaks on a smooth continuum match the fitted model; with ~1e5 counts the statistical error of the mean over 30+ realisations is < 0.1 %, so a bias > 1 % is a systematic defect of the area estimator.
Centroid precision for 1e5-count peaks is ~FWHM/(2.355*sqrt(N)) ~ 0.001 FWHM; 0.02 FWHM allows for channel-integration effects only.
The engine's FWHM model is rescaled to strong isolated peaks; it must reproduce the true width to 5 % (a 5 % width error already biases constrained-width areas by ~1-2 %).
Reported 1-sigma area uncertainties must have nominal coverage (binomial band, n >= 200).
Same as above for 2 sigma.
No invented separation: a true singlet reported as two or more peaks within 1 FWHM in more than 5 % of cases means the doublet retry fires on noise.

Strong peaks with a 4 % low-energy tail, fitted with the shape calibration of the detector: the statistical sd is ~0.3 %; the tail must no longer bias the area (uncalibrated baseline -1.05 % HPGe, -1.42 % NaI).
The stated area uncertainties must cover the error for tailed peaks (baseline 0.78 / 0.03).
The tail must not become a second peak.
Unmatched peaks per spectrum stay at the strong-peak level (baseline ~1).
Reported only.
Residual search on top of the tail model (protocol amendment 3): unmatched peaks may rise by at most 0.1 per spectrum over the baseline 1.0.
A shape calibration measured on a detector without a tail must not bias Gaussian peaks (same limit as the strong-peak area criterion).
At s = 7 the expected detection probability is ~0.99 for an efficient search.
At s = 5 the expected detection probability is ~0.8; below 0.5 the search wastes sensitivity relative to its own threshold.
Near the threshold; recorded to compare future search improvements (no limit: the trade-off against false peaks is set by the false-peak criterion).
For s >= 7 detection selection bias is small; a mean area bias > 5 % is systematic.
Pure Poisson continuum: a 3-sigma one-sided threshold gives ~1.35 false peaks per 1000 independent resolution elements; 3 allows for Poisson tails and correlated trials.
Separation >= 1.5 FWHM with intensity ratio <= 3 is visibly two peaks; both must be found.
Component areas of resolved doublets (s >= 30 each) must be unbiased within 5 %.
Two equal peaks 1 FWHM apart still show a flat top / inflection that a joint fit should resolve in most realisations (counts >= 2e4 per component).
Unresolvable doublets need not be split, but the multiplet's total area must be conserved (sum of reported peaks within the multiplet window).
The residual search must not split peaks: reported peaks in the multiplet window beyond the matched ones.
Adding a satellite component must not distort the strong (1e5 counts) peak's area.
Satellites of 1e4 counts beside a 1e5-count peak: area within 10 % when found.
A 1 % satellite may be below the statistical limit; reported only.
With the tail modelled, the residual search must not split tailed peaks.  NaI: no search (low resolution), reported only.
A satellite component must not take area from the tailed main peak.
The satellite must not absorb the main peak's tail.
Same limit as the Gaussian case: the tail model must not hide satellites.
Splitting peaks < 0.75 FWHM apart is reported only: claiming it automatically is not required and can be a sign of over-fitting.
Peaks with s >= 20 on a Compton edge must still be found.
Linear background + step under a peak on an edge: 5 % allows for continuum-shape mismatch.
The edge itself must not be reported as a peak in more than 1 of 5 spectra.
Peaks carry a low-energy exponential tail with 4 % of the area; an estimator that recovers at least a quarter of the tail stays within 3 %.  Larger bias means tailed peaks lose area.
A tail must not be reported as a separate peak.
Peaks of 100-400 counts on ~1-3 counts/channel: Poisson regime.  Neyman-weighted least squares is known to bias low here; > 5 % average bias is a defect worth fixing.
Uncertainty coverage in the low-count regime (wider band: fewer matched peaks).
Engine contract (analysis/__init__.py): < 0.5 s per spectrum for interactive use.
Fraction of present nuclides (strongest line s >= 15) reported.  NaI lower: merged lines make some nuclides legitimately ambiguous.
Reported nuclides that are absent (aliases of the same decay chain count as present).
Recall vs. deliberate gain error (0, 0.1, 0.3, 1 %): informational, no a-priori limit.
Same spectra searched with the environmental application library (the GUI default): informational; the scored criteria keep the full library for comparability.
Recall with the environmental library, over present nuclides that belong to it.

A source spectrum with strong lines (HPGe: Eu-152 with a mildly non-linear true calibration; NaI: Am-241 + Cs-137 + Co-60) must give a calibration within 0.1 FWHM over the calibrated range.  0.1 FWHM keeps identification windows (~0.5 FWHM) unaffected.
A spectrum of Co-60 + Cs-137 presented as 'Eu-152' must not produce an unflagged calibration (an exception or a failed validation both count as flagged).
Natural-background spectrum whose stored gain is wrong by 0.3 % (HPGe) / 1 % (NaI), i.e. >= 0.2 FWHM at 1460 keV: the drift check must report it.
No drift: the check must stay quiet in at least 95 % of spectra.
The proposed correction, once accepted, must bring the calibration within 0.1 FWHM over the range of the background lines used.
Detection fraction per drift level (0, 0.1, 0.3, 1 %): informational.
